subject: Re: Implementation and Migration Questionnaire — pivotless rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Peter Chung <peter.chung@globalbank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: GlobalBank Migration Team <migration@globalbank.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation questionnaire: timeline, integration steps, and canary tactics

Aditya,

Thanks for the RFI response earlier this week. The procurement and cloud migration teams asked me to pull together a focused set of follow-ups specifically on the deployment/migration plan portion of your submission. To move the SOW and security review forward we need: a week-by-week timeline, a short description of integration steps (auth, data flow, network requirements), a clearly scoped canary/validation path that minimizes risk to production, and an explicit rollback plan.

Particularly:
- Expected downtime (if any) for initial switchover and subsequent cutover windows
- How you handle KV cache priming and prefix caching when traffic is switched
- What metrics you need us to surface during canary (latency p95, error rate, token-cost delta, sample outputs)
- Who is expected to be on-call from Redwood during critical windows

Can you send a concise migration questionnaire response and a proposed 6-week timeline by COB Tuesday? We want to include it in the architecture review on Thursday.

Thanks,
Peter Chung
Lead, Enterprise Cloud Migration
GlobalBank
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chung <peter.chung@globalbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-29T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questionnaire: timeline, integration steps, and canary tactics

Peter —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are two artifacts: a one-page "pivotless rollout" overview that focuses on staged traffic shifts without a hard cutover, and a sequenced rollback plan spreadsheet. High-level answers below; we've kept the timeline conservative but can compress with stakeholder sign-off.

Proposed 6-week timeline (high level):
- Week 0: Pre-kick, networking & credentials exchange, mutual TLS cert handoff, firewalls / peering checks
- Week 1: Non-prod integration: API keys, sample traffic, validate auth & routes
- Week 2: Shadow traffic & metrics validation (traffic mirroring only)
- Week 3: Small canary (1% traffic) with KV cache warming and sampling validation; run quality evals on prompt set A
- Week 4: Incremental ramp (1% -> 10% -> 25%) across 3 days with rollback gates
- Week 5: Full routing for non-critical routes; begin mixed-route acceptance tests
- Week 6: Production cutover for configured routes; post-cutover monitoring window & runbook closeout

Downtime: Our approach aims for zero planned downtime for inference calls — traffic is gradually shifted using routing policies and prefix/KV cache warming. Short (~1-2 minute) maintenance windows may be needed for control-plane changes (routing policy toggles) in case of emergency.

KV cache priming: we recommend a 24-48 hour warmup window during shadowing. We surface warmed key hit-rate and a cache-priming progress metric.

Canary metrics (minimum):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (per-route)
- Error rate (5xx and API-level failures)
- Token cost per request (avg and delta vs baseline)
- Output quality checks: BLEU-style diffs for structured outputs + thresholded heuristics for hallucination score on sample prompts

On-call: Redwood will provide a named on-call engineer + product lead for each critical window; we will share escalation matrix.

Next steps: we can present this at your architecture review Thursday at 10:30 PT. If that works I will circulate the attachments and a meeting invite.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chung <peter.chung@globalbank.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-30T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questionnaire: timeline, integration steps, and canary tactics

Peter / Aditya — quick technical notes to supplement the timeline above (copy of the runbook attached for details):

1) Authentication & network
- Primary model: mutual TLS between GlobalBank edge and Redwood private endpoints (we can fall back to token-based with IP allowlist for proof-of-concept).
- No DB schema changes required on your side — Redwood's inference endpoints operate as a stateless front with optional persistent KV for caching (we only persist cache keys if customer opts in).

2) KV cache & prefix behavior
- Cache is sharded per-customer. During ramp we will pre-warm the cache by replaying anonymized sample traffic; cache hydration progress is exposed via the console API.
- If you prefer isolated warm-up we can run a pre-fill job using non-prod traffic and controlled prompts.

3) Routing & fallback
- We will use workload-aware routing: canary traffic goes to an isolated variant (quantized model if requested) with automatic fallback to baseline model on higher-than-threshold error rate or latency regression
- We support traffic split percentages as low as 0.1% for very granular testing

4) Rollback mechanics
- Rolling back is a control-plane operation: we change route weights back to baseline and invalidate any warmed cache for the new variant to avoid inconsistent outputs; expected rollback RTO < 5 minutes for routing-only rollbacks.

5) Observability hooks
- We will provide per-token cost telemetry, tracing spans to correlate upstream request IDs, and a streaming callback to your analytics endpoint for near-real-time validation.

Attach: runbook + rollback spreadsheet. Happy to deep-dive on Friday if the architecture review requires an engineering breakout.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Peter Chung <peter.chung@globalbank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: migration@globalbank.com
Date: 2027-08-31T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questionnaire: timeline, integration steps, and canary tactics

Aditya / Laura — this is the level of detail we needed, thank you. A few clarifying points from the architecture board:

- We require an explicit dry-run plan where we mirror 100% of a subset of traffic for 48 hours and apply the exact production prompt set (no sampling). Can you confirm Redwood supports full traffic mirroring with zero request-side modification?
- For rollback: the board wants an explicit test that proves rollback will not corrupt session state for any in-flight requests. Can you describe the test and timing?
- On-call coverage: we prefer a Named Engineer + Named Product contact for all ramp steps (not an alias). Please provide names and mobile contact for the Thursday review.

If you can send answers by EOD Wednesday we will greenlight the SOW to legal for doc prep.

—Peter
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chung <peter.chung@globalbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questionnaire: timeline, integration steps, and canary tactics

Peter — quick confirmations and concrete next items ahead of Thursday's architecture review: 

1) Traffic mirroring: yes, Redwood supports full request mirroring for selected routes. Mirror is synchronous-for-observability (we do not alter original request path) and can be configured for 48-hour windows with payload fidelity preserved. We will provide guidance on sampling, but can run the exact prompt set with identical inputs.

2) Rollback safety test: our recommended test is a live rollback rehearsal during the incremental ramp where we intentionally fail a tiny percentage of canary requests and trigger the rollback control-plane change. We validate (a) no orphaned KV entries, (b) in-flight inference requests receive either a baseline response or a well-defined failure code (we will add a short-lived error wrapper to detect mismatches), and (c) end-to-end request tracing shows no duplicated side-effects. We can run the rehearsal during the 1%->10% step (Week 4 in the proposed timeline) — expected RTO < 5 minutes, full validation within 30 minutes.

3) Named contacts:
- On-call engineer: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.ai, +1-415-555-0147)
- Product lead: Priyom Das (priyom_das@redwood.ai, +1-650-555-0213)

4) Docs & next steps: attached updated runbook includes the dry-run checklist and rehearsal script. I will send the architecture review invite for Thursday 10:30 PT and drop the HubSpot deal link + DocuSign SOW stub into the meeting notes. Once the architecture review signs off we will ask legal to process the SOW and schedule the pre-kick call.

Thanks — looking forward to the review.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
